- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_app_state({ include_schema: true, include_canvas_design: true, include_scripts_and_shaders: false }) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. All three flags are required. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_app_state, get_guidelines, execute, get_screenshot, export_nodes, export_html.
Also: browser.

- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- releases: CipherBox v2 release and staging-deploy mechanics — release-please layout, the two version surfaces, staging tag pipeline, and the v1 freeze. Use when cutting a release, deploying to staging, or touching release/versioning config.
- crypto-privacy-review: Review code for cryptographic security, generate test cases and edge cases
- resolve-pr-reviews: Resolve PR Review Comments
- ship: Ship
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Held as a draft: **blocked on UAT, which is blocked on #1253.**

CI is green and CodeRabbit's verdict on `71e1d1405` is clean. What is outstanding is not a code review — it is the one claim in this PR that only a human at a browser can settle, and settling it needs a working login.

## What is unverified

Whether an ordinary browser saves the **file's own bytes** or the app shell. `useFileDownload` mints a `/stream/<ticket>` URL and clicks an anchor; if the Service Worker does not intercept that request, the origin answers it with the SPA fallback and the member receives a 394-byte `index.html` under the file's name, with no error surfaced. Filed as #1247.

It cannot be settled inside Playwright, because Playwright's own CDP download capture is the suspect. It needs a real browser, a real session, DevTools open, and a check that the worker is **controlling** the page before the click — if it is not, `MediaService.streaming` is false, `streamTicket` returns null, and `save` quietly takes the buffered blob path, which works correctly and proves nothing about the path under suspicion.

## Why it is blocked

Login is down on every method. Google returns `401 invalid_client` because the Web3Auth project client ID is passed where the provider's belongs; wallet dead-ends at `NotStarted`; passwordless email is Web3Auth's rather than ours. All three are #1253, and the Google half specifically is #1256 — the one piece that is independent of the ADR and can land on its own.

## What this PR does not depend on

Nothing here rests on that verification. The round trip asserts through the preview path (buffered `facade.download`) rather than the save affordance, precisely because the save path is under suspicion — so the byte assertion never touches it. #1247 records that the workaround should be removed once the save path is trusted.

Flip back to ready once a session can be created and the check is run.

content.content: {"baseRefName":"main","body":"> **Held as a draft — blocked on UAT, which is blocked on #1253.** > CI is green and the CodeRabbit verdict on the head is clean. The one outstanding > claim is whether an ordinary browser saves the file's bytes or the app shell > (#1247), and settling it needs a working login, which no method currently has. > Nothing in this PR depends on that check — the byte assertion goes through the > preview path, not the save affordance. Closes #1096 Closes #1153 Two CI-owned slices in one PR: they share no file. ## The web e2e write path `web-e2e.yml` gains an `ipfs/kubo` service mirroring the contract job, plus the two variables the write path needs: - `KUBO_API_URL` — without it `KuboPinStore` refuses every hosted upload with a 503, and since PR #1217 the drain charges that as a spent attempt, so a write spec would dead-letter rather than fail on an assertion. - `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL` pointed at the same stack's gateway. This one is not optional either: the drain's rebase leg reads the record head block back before it publishes onto it, and with no content source configured the queue never drains at all. It is addressed as `127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`, because Kubo serves `localhost` as a *subdomain* gateway and 301s every path request to `.ipfs.localhost`, which resolves nowhere in a browser. Five new specs in `tests/web-e2e/tests/write-path.spec.ts`, bound to shipped `data-testid`s and shipped accessible names — folder create, rename, move and delete, and an upload read back byte for byte through the preview. Two deliberate shapes: - Every case ends on a **drained queue with no dead letter**. "The row is on screen" is the optimistic overlay and would pass over a write that never published. - Each assertion queues a **probe folder behind the write under test**. The op queue is strict FIFO, so the probe's pending mark clears only once everything ahead of it published — otherwise a delete or a move out takes its own row off the root and leaves the settle nothing to wait on. The `e2e` project now takes every spec except the bundle-shape one, so a new spec joins the gate the day it lands instead of when someone remembers to widen a list. `retries: 0` is untouched: the suite ran 78/78 green locally across six repeats of the full file. `tests/web-e2e/README.md` loses the "does not cover yet" section, which is now false, and its local recipe gains Kubo and both variables. ## Seeding the cargo caches from main `ci.yml` triggers on `pull_request` only, and GitHub scopes a cache entry to the ref that wrote it, so every PR's first cargo run was cold on every cargo job. A run *can* read entries scoped to the default branch, so a new `Cargo Cache Seed` workflow writes two of them on main-push and the PR jobs gain a trailing restore-key that reaches them: | seed entry | serves | | --- | --- | | `main-cargo-` | `linux-cargo-`, `core-kats-cargo-`, `client-browser-cargo-` | | `main-wasm-cargo-` | `wasm-engine-cargo-`, `web-e2e-cargo-` | Two entries rather than one per job prefix, because the repo's cache budget is already over the limit and these have to earn their bytes against the PR-scoped entries LRU evicts. The keys hash `Cargo.lock` plus `rust-toolchain.toml` — the two inputs that invalidate a dependency tree — so a merge that changes neither hits its own key and writes nothing at all; the trigger is narrowed to the same two files. A weekly cron and `workflow_dispatch` cover an entry evicted between lockfile changes. macOS, Windows and the desktop matrix are deliberately not seeded: they would add four more multi-GB entries on the most expensive runners. ## Verification - `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` — all clean. - `zizmor --no-online-audits .github/workflows/ .github/actions/` (the pinned 1.25.2) — no findings; the new workflow is not added to any ignore list. - `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e --repeat-each=6` against a live local stack — 78 passed. ## Found on the way, not fixed here Two runtime findings outside this PR's files, both reproducible: - **Saving a file to disk silently writes the wrong bytes.** `useFileDownload` mints a `/stream/` URL and clicks an anchor at it; the Service Worker does not intercept that request, so the origin answers with the SPA fallback and the user gets a 394-byte `index.html` under the file's name, with no error surfaced. Reproduced 3/3. This is why the round trip asserts through the preview — the buffered read — rather than through the save. - **A second forced refresh while a pass is in flight displaces it**, and the queue drains on neither; polling the footer's refresh control at 1 Hz kept a single queued folder create unpublished for over 60 s, while one click settles it in ~1.8 s. The suite works around it by forcing exactly one pass and then waiting passively. Also worth wiring by whoever owns `apps/web`: `engineHostConfig` never sets `profile`, so a `VITE_ENVIRONMENT=ci` bundle runs the production 30 s poll cadence rather than the CI profile's 1 s. That is what makes the forced-pass workaround necessary at all. > [!NOTE] > ### Add web E2E write-path tests and seed Cargo caches from main branch > - Adds a new [cargo-cache-seed.yml](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1246/files#diff-de0a938b1387cf04a8ed1fc581b6d318e68975ac985f2c9dbd37cb914cdcb1a6) workflow that builds native and WASM targets on pushes to `main` and weekly, populating `main-cargo-` and `main-wasm-cargo-` cache keys as fallbacks for PR builds. > - Updates CI and web-e2e workflows to fall back to these main-branch caches on cache misses, reducing cold-build times on PRs. > - Adds a local IPFS (Kubo) service to [web-e2e.yml](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1246/files#diff-4efe558d3ea6a7f6f4d2fe62ea60c812c4dc61ec3cfde6998833f3e1d2e4d71d) with `KUBO_API_URL` and `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL` env vars wired for tests. > - Adds a [write-path.spec.ts](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1246/files#diff-36de243b8da1de703af7df6c96ca3bd1f84d3e4a82a3fa38fa8c11f738c0d5ee) E2E suite covering folder create/rename/move/delete and file upload, verifying content via UI preview and direct engine readback using a new `window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__.download` introspection hook. > - Expands the Playwright e2e project from only `smoke.spec.ts` to all tests except `release-bundle.spec.ts`. > > > > Macroscope summarized 71e1d14. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added support for creating, renaming, moving, and deleting folders and files. - Added file upload, preview, and download validation, including multiline and multibyte content. - Added hosted storage integration for upload and retrieval testing. - Added reliable file-content retrieval through the web engine. - **Bug Fixes** - Improved test reliability by waiting for vault updates and completed operations. - Expanded failure handling when storage services are unavailable. - **Documentation** - Updated web testing setup and documented supported file-management workflows. name: web-e2e-local-full-suite-recipe
description: "How to get a trustworthy local full web-e2e run — env alignment, fresh dev servers, and the two known external failure signatures"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 064836b9-90e4-42d5-aabc-ed5fde831a57
---

Running the full 208-spec `tests/web-e2e` suite locally (learned 2026-07-03, phase 68.1 exit gates):

- **API env**: the API dev process MUST export `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production` (the sdk-e2e harness default) — a mismatched/other value 401s `recovery.spec.ts` and any test-login caller, masking their real state. Start: `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://localhost:3001 pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api dev`.
- **Fresh dev servers**: restart vite (and rebuild `sdk-core`/`sdk` dists first) before a gate run — a multi-day vite process caused roving `wallet-login-button` timeouts; vite also serves stale sdk code after dist rebuilds unless restarted.
- **Web3Auth Core Kit external flake** (~2-3 files per full run, roving): signatures are the login-page toast `Failed to get vault keypair from Core Kit` and a raw Torus quorum banner `Unable to resolve enough promises`. NOT our code — `wallet-login-helpers.ts` has bounded retry (68.1-25/29), but it can still exceed the budget. Disposition: single-file re-run once; green = external flake.
- **Serial cascade**: every spec file is `describe.serial` — one failure skips the rest of its file ("N did not run" ≠ global abort). Judge coverage by first-failures per file + single-file re-runs, not the raw did-not-run count.
- **Capture discipline**: redirect the run to a log and append `EXIT_CODE=$?`; never pipe through `tail`/`tee` (masks exit codes). Playwright wipes `test-results/` per run — harvest failure screenshots BEFORE any re-run. This config writes no usable `.last-run.json` for full runs — don't build watchdogs on it.
- Full run ≈ 17-20 min (M-series, workers=1). Related: [[bg-executor-lost-wake-continuation]] — executors that background the suite run may lose their wake; nudge via SendMessage with the tally.

name: project-local-login-config-from-gh-actions-vars
description: "The Web3Auth and Google login config for local UAT lives in GitHub Actions variables, not in any committed file"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ff3a17b8-94b6-4c1b-94ab-5253b0600f57
  modified: 2026-08-16T13:38:21.323Z
---

No committed file holds the Web3Auth or Google identifiers a local interactive
login needs. Read them from the repo's GitHub Actions variables instead of
asking the user:

- `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/actions/variables` gives
  `VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `REDACTED`.
- `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/environments/staging/variables`
  gives a `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` that already lists `tauri://localhost`.

The project's real Google client is
`164556913424-uif44is1apnl7rqc9a2ac7vn8u9dq0ee`, which holds `localhost:5173`,
`app-staging.cipherbox.cc`, `cipher-box.onrender.com`, `localhost:1420` and the
three `http://127.0.0.1:1420{0,1,2}/callback` entries.

Until 2026-08-16 the staging `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` variable named
`959751863260-j1u1…` instead — a client that rejects both
`https://app-staging.cipherbox.cc` and the desktop loopback URI, so staging
Google sign-in failed with `redirect_uri_mismatch`. The variable is now
corrected, but a redeploy is what makes it take effect.

`desktop-staging-release.yml` feeds `vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` into
`VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, so web and desktop use one Google client.
`VITE_ENVIRONMENT=local` maps to `WEB3AUTH_NETWORK.DEVNET`, the network those
variables belong to.

**Why:** the values are variables rather than secrets, so they are readable, and
guessing or asking wastes a round trip.

**How to apply:** for a desktop or web local login run, pull the four values
this way. `apps/api/.env` must also carry `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and list
`tauri://localhost` in `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, or the identity exchange from a
packaged Tauri webview is refused. See
[[project-desktop-uat-stack-recipe]].

name: feedback-leave-docker-stack-running
description: "Don't tear down the shared cipherbox docker stack after ship/e2e — leave it running"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 60afe4f5-90e8-4017-b046-ab86ca19c540
---

After a ship/e2e run, do NOT bring down the `cipherbox-infrastructure` docker
compose stack (`docker/docker-compose.yml`: ipfs/kubo, someguy, postgres, redis,
mock-ipns-routing) or standalone dev containers like `byo-ipfs-kubo`. Only clean
up session-specific processes you started — e.g. the ship-started API-from-dist
on :3000.

**Why:** the docker stack is shared infrastructure that other sessions/processes
may be using; tearing it down disrupts them and forces a slow rebuild/restart.

**How to apply:** on cleanup, `kill` the :3000 API (and any other process this
session spawned) but leave `docker compose down` out of it unless the user
explicitly asks to stop docker. Relates to [[project-web-e2e-local-full-suite-recipe]].

name: project-api-restart-masked-by-eaddrinuse
description: A failed local API restart is masked because the old process keeps serving port 3000 and answers the health check
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ff3a17b8-94b6-4c1b-94ab-5253b0600f57
  modified: 2026-08-14T12:47:48.798Z
---

`pkill -f 'nest start'` does not stop the local API. The process command is
`node -r ts-node/register src/main.ts`, so the pattern matches nothing. The new
process then dies with `EADDRINUSE` on port 3000 while the **old** one keeps
answering `/health` with `{"status":"ok"}`, so the restart looks successful and
the new configuration never takes effect.

This cost a debugging cycle on 2026-08-14: a stale API kept an old
`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` from an inline environment override, and every Google login
died at `google-oauth.service.ts:51` with the generic
`Google token verification failed`, which names no audience.

**Why:** a health check proves that *something* serves the port, never that it
is the process just started.

**How to apply:** stop with `pkill -f 'ts-node/register src/main.ts'`. After any
restart, assert the listener changed — `lsof -nP -iTCP:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN -t` —
and grep the log for `EADDRINUSE`. Prefer editing `apps/api/.env` over an inline
override, because an override outlives the file and is invisible in it.

# Web E2E

The PR gate's smoke slice: `apps/web` driven in a real browser against a real
API, a real engine, and the hermetic `/routing/v1` record store. Wired as the
merge-blocking `Web E2E Smoke` job (`.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml`), reported
through the stable `Web E2E Smoke Result` context in `ci.yml`.

Normative source: [`blueprint/testing.md`](../../blueprint/testing.md).

## What it covers

- the front door renders every built login method
- an unauthenticated deep link is returned to the front door and lists no vault
  contents
- a cold start reaches a settled, empty vault at its root; the chrome renders
  it, and the event taps saw the snapshot that produced it
- signing out returns the tab to the front door
- the shipping bundle exposes no introspection hook

## What it does not cover yet

Nothing on the write path — no folder create/rename/move/delete, no upload, no
download. `blueprint/testing.md` scopes this tier at login-and-CRUD, and the
CRUD half is blocked on engine and workflow work outside this suite. The issue
tracker carries what is outstanding and why.

## How the suite logs in

There is no interactive Core Kit login in CI. The `e2e` build carries the
introspection hook (`apps/web/src/engine/introspection.ts`), which hands the
engine a login secret the test generates. Challenge-signature login creates the
account on first contact, so each test's fresh 32-byte secret is a fresh,
isolated vault — no fixture setup and no shared state to serialize around.

The `release` project runs the same specs' counterpart against a bundle built
**without** the flag, and asserts `window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__` is absent.

## Running it locally

Both bundles must be built before Playwright starts; the config only serves
them.

1. Bring up Postgres and the record store:

   ```sh
   docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d postgres mock-ipns-routing
   ```

2. Apply migrations and boot the API:

   ```sh
   export DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5432 DB_USERNAME=postgres \
     DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED DB_DATABASE=cipherbox NODE_ENV=test \
     JWT_SECRET=web-e2e-jwt-secret THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT=200 \
     CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:4173,http://localhost:4174
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build && node apps/api/dist/main.js
   ```

3. Build both bundles:

   ```sh
   export VITE_ENVIRONMENT=ci VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \
     VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS=http://localhost:3001
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:wasm
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
   mv apps/web/dist apps/web/dist-release
   VITE_E2E_HOOK=true pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
   ```

4. Run the suite:

   ```sh
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e
   ```

   The script is `test:e2e`, not `test`: the workspace-wide `Test` gate runs no
   suite that needs a live stack.

Rebuild the bundle after any `apps/web` change — the suite serves `dist/`, not
a dev server.

26	Use the v2 ubiquitous language defined in `CONTEXT.md` — every domain term (scope, epoch, ascent link, grant blob, adoption gate, floor law, eager set, …) has exactly one name there. General conventions: `publicKey`/`privateKey`/`ipnsName`/`ipnsRecord` spelled out in full camelCase for API fields, snake_case for database columns.
27	
28	## Critical Security Rules
29	
30	1. **Never** store `privateKey` or any seed in localStorage/sessionStorage
31	2. **Never** log sensitive keys or seeds
32	3. **Never** send unencrypted keys to the server — the server is zero-knowledge and NEVER sees plaintext or unencrypted keys
33	4. **All crypto lives in `crates/core`** — TypeScript has no codec or crypto of its own; never implement crypto in TS
34	5. Primitives are fixed by `blueprint/core.md`: XChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing, BLAKE3 tree KDF, X25519 + HPKE key wrapping, REDACTED signing — no key derives outside the frozen KDF edge catalog
35	6. Every resolved record passes the adoption gate; a failure is a fail-closed trust violation, never mere staleness
36	7. Clear sensitive material from memory after use (zeroize at the terminal owner only — a callee must not zero caller-owned buffers)
37	8. **Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry** — when a decode/verify path hard-rejects an invariant violation (a trust/malformed check), the matching encode/produce path MUST enforce the same invariant with a **release-active** check that returns `Err` — never `debug_assert!`/`assert!`, which are stripped in release. Otherwise a release build can sign and publish bytes its own decoder always rejects (an unopenable ledger/commitment/body). Keep these encode-side checks consistent with the `crates/core/src/seal/body.rs` `assert_children_unique` convention, and cover them with a test that fires in a release build.
38	
39	## API Contract and Clients
40	
41	There are **no generated API clients** and no codegen loop. The engine contains the single hand-written Rust API client; the NestJS API's OpenAPI document is a committed docs artifact, not a build input. The contract is enforced by the live contract-test suite (the sdk-e2e descendant) running the real client against a real API instance on every PR — see `blueprint/testing.md`.

content.content:
# Web E2E

The PR gate's smoke slice: `apps/web` driven in a real browser against a real
API, a real engine, and the hermetic `/routing/v1` record store. Wired as the
merge-blocking `Web E2E Smoke` job (`.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml`), reported
through the stable `Web E2E Smoke Result` context in `ci.yml`.

Normative source: [`blueprint/testing.md`](../../blueprint/testing.md).

## What it covers

- the front door renders every built login method
- an unauthenticated deep link is returned to the front door and lists no vault
  contents
- a cold start reaches a settled, empty vault at its root; the chrome renders
  it, and the event taps saw the snapshot that produced it
- folder create, rename, move and delete, each ending on a drained queue that
  carries no dead letter — so a write that never published fails the gate
- an upload and the file read back off the network, asserted byte for byte
- signing out returns the tab to the front door
- the shipping bundle exposes no introspection hook

## How the suite logs in

There is no interactive Core Kit login in CI. The `e2e` build carries the
introspection hook (`apps/web/src/engine/introspection.ts`), which hands the
engine a login secret the test generates. Challenge-signature login creates the
account on first contact, so each test's fresh 32-byte secret is a fresh,
isolated vault — no fixture setup and no shared state to serialize around.

The `release` project runs the same specs' counterpart against a bundle built
**without** the flag, and asserts `window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__` is absent.

## Running it locally

Both bundles must be built before Playwright starts; the config only serves
them.

1. Bring up Postgres, Kubo and the record store:

   ```sh
   docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d postgres ipfs mock-ipns-routing
   ```

2. Apply migrations and boot the API:

   ```sh
   export DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5432 DB_USERNAME=postgres \
     DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED DB_DATABASE=cipherbox NODE_ENV=test \
     JWT_SECRET=web-e2e-jwt-secret THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT=200 \
     KUBO_API_URL=http://localhost:5001 \
     CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:4173,http://localhost:4174
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build && node apps/api/dist/main.js
   ```

   Without `KUBO_API_URL` the API refuses every hosted upload with a 503, and
   the write specs dead-letter rather than fail on an assertion.

3. Build both bundles:

   ```sh
   export VITE_ENVIRONMENT=ci VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \
     VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS=http://localhost:3001 \
     VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:wasm
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
   mv apps/web/dist apps/web/dist-release
   VITE_E2E_HOOK=true pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
   ```

4. Run the suite:

   ```sh
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e
   ```

   The script is `test:e2e`, not `test`: the workspace-wide `Test` gate runs no
   suite that needs a live stack.

Rebuild the bundle after any `apps/web` change — the suite serves `dist/`, not
a dev server.

001-provide-strategy.sh
---
#!/bin/sh
# CipherBox Kubo init: announce only pin roots to the DHT, not every block.
#
# Reduces background provide/reprovide CPU on the shared Kubo node. With the
# default "all" strategy the staging node scheduled ~76k CIDs for DHT
# announcement, consuming a large share of Kubo's CPU at idle; "roots" cuts that
# to the pin-root count (~18k) with no loss of retrievability (every pinned root
# is still announced; only unpinned intermediate blocks are dropped).
#
# Kubo 0.40 renamed Reprovider.Strategy -> Provide.Strategy. This file is sourced
# by the Kubo entrypoint on every boot (before the daemon starts), so the setting
# is idempotent and survives container recreation and fresh repos.
ipfs config Provide.Strategy roots || echo "ipfs-init: failed to set Provide.Strategy roots (continuing)"
=== compose ipfs/kubo service ===
name: cipherbox-infrastructure
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: cipherbox-postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE:-cipherbox}
    ports:
      - '${DB_PORT:-5432}:5432'
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U postgres']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  ipfs:
    image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
    container_name: cipherbox-ipfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - IPFS_PATH=/data/ipfs
      # pebbleds: LSM-tree datastore for faster concurrent write throughput (Phase 19.2)
      # Requires fresh IPFS repo -- delete ipfs_data volume before first start:
      #   docker compose down -v --remove-orphans && docker compose up -d
      - IPFS_PROFILE=server,pebbleds
    volumes:
      - ipfs_data:/data/ipfs
      # Kubo runs /container-init.d/*.sh on every boot (sourced before the daemon);
      # 001-provide-strategy.sh sets Provide.Strategy=roots idempotently.
      - ./ipfs-init:/container-init.d:ro
    ports:
      # Swarm - P2P connections
      - '4001:4001/tcp'
      - '4001:4001/udp'
      # TODO: Create environment-specific configs for staging/prod with:
      #   - 127.0.0.1 bindings or reverse proxy with authentication
      #   - IPFS API auth enabled
      # API - bound to all interfaces for dev (VM/host access)
      - '5001:5001'
      # Gateway - bound to all interfaces for dev (VM/host access)
      - '8080:8080'
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'ipfs id || exit 1']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          # Kubo is load-bearing; mirror the staging tuning (see docs/CAPACITY.md).
          memory: 3G
          cpus: '1.5'

  someguy:
    image: ghcr.io/ipfs/someguy:v0.11.1
    container_name: cipherbox-someguy
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      SOMEGUY_LISTEN_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:8190
      SOMEGUY_DHT: accelerated
      SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_CONNMGR_LOW: 100
      SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_CONNMGR_HIGH: 3000
      SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY: 1073741824
      GOLOG_LOG_LEVEL: info
      GOLOG_LOG_FMT: json
    ports:
      # HTTP API for delegated routing
      - '8190:8190'
      # libp2p swarm - required for DHT participation
      - '4004:4004/tcp'
      - '4004:4004/udp'
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'curl -sf http://localhost:8190/version || exit 1']
      interval: 10s

content.content:
# The web e2e smoke slice (blueprint/testing.md). The suite runs against the
# production static build, so it needs the engine WASM: a caller passes
# `wasm-artifact` to hand over the module its run already built, and a caller
# that does not gets the module built here. It builds the bundle twice: once as
# it ships, once with `VITE_E2E_HOOK` for the introspection seam. The suite
# asserts the shipping one carries no hook.
name: Web E2E Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to checkout (tag, branch, or SHA)'
        required: false
        type: string
      wasm-artifact:
        description: >-
          Name of a run artifact holding a prebuilt engine WASM module. Set it
          and the suite tests exactly those bytes; leave it empty and this job
          builds the module itself, which is what a standalone dispatch needs.
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string

permissions: {}

jobs:
  web-e2e:
    name: Web E2E Smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The suite itself runs in seconds; the budget covers a standalone
    # dispatch, where a cold-cache wasm build runs ahead of it.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      # The write path's block store. Without it `KuboPinStore` refuses every
      # hosted upload with a 503, which the drain charges as a spent attempt —
      # so a write spec dead-letters rather than merely failing to publish.
      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s

    env:
      DB_HOST: localhost
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USERNAME: postgres
      DB_PASSWORD: postgres
      DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
      JWT_SECRET: web-e2e-jwt-secret
      KUBO_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
      # Every test cold-starts its own account from one runner IP, so the
      # per-IP auth bucket would otherwise cap how many specs can exist.
      THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT: '200'
      CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: http://localhost:4173,http://localhost:4174
      # `ci` names no deployment, so the bundle needs no Web3Auth identifiers:
      # the suite hands the engine a login secret through the introspection seam
      # rather than through an interactive Core Kit session.
      VITE_ENVIRONMENT: ci
      VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
      # The hermetic record store, in place of the public default — a merge gate
      # must not resolve vault pointers over the internet.
      VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS: http://localhost:3001
      # The same stack's gateway, so a read pulls its blocks back from where the
      # upload pinned them rather than from the tab that wrote them. By address,
      # not by name: Kubo serves `localhost` as a *subdomain* gateway and 301s
      # every path request to `<cid>.ipfs.localhost`, which resolves nowhere.
      VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}

      # Fail fast on a missing or malformed handover, before the stack boots.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: inputs.wasm-artifact != ''
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wasm-artifact }}
          path: apps/web/src/wasm

      # Same path set as `ci.yml`'s `Web Engine WASM` cache, for the same reason.
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: inputs.wasm-artifact == ''
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target/release
            target/wasm32-unknown-unknown
          key: web-e2e-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            web-e2e-cargo-
            main-wasm-cargo-

      - uses: ./.github/actions/wasm-bindgen-cli
        if: inputs.wasm-artifact == ''

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - uses: ./.github/actions/mock-ipns-routing

      # `NODE_ENV` stays on the API's own steps. Vite reads it to decide whether a
      # build is a production one, so job-wide it would hand the suite a
      # development bundle of the app it is meant to test as it ships.
      - name: Apply migrations to a fresh database
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
        env:
          NODE_ENV: test

      - name: Build and boot the API
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
          node apps/api/dist/main.js > /tmp/api.log 2>&1 &
          curl -fsS --retry 60 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 http://localhost:3000/health \
            || { echo '--- API log ---'; cat /tmp/api.log; exit 1; }
        env:
          NODE_ENV: test

      # One engine module feeds both bundles below; only the hook flag differs
      # between them.
      - name: Build the engine WASM
        if: inputs.wasm-artifact == ''
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:wasm

      - name: Build the shipping bundle
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
          mv apps/web/dist apps/web/dist-release

      - name: Build the e2e bundle
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
        env:
          VITE_E2E_HOOK: 'true'

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e exec playwright install --with-deps chromium

      # Named `test:e2e`, not `test`: the workspace-wide `Test` gate runs no
      # suite that needs a live stack.
      - name: Run the web e2e smoke slice
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e

      - name: Upload the Playwright report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: web-e2e-report
          path: |
            tests/web-e2e/playwright-report/
            tests/web-e2e/test-results/
          retention-days: 7

# CipherBox web app — local development template.
#
# Copy to apps/web/.env. Vite reads it at BUILD time, so rebuild after editing.
# Every name below is read by the code; the commented ones are genuinely
# optional and are left unset on purpose.

VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
VITE_ENVIRONMENT=local

# Where the engine resolves and publishes records. Must name the same backend
# as the API's ROUTING_V1_URL, or the republisher re-PUTs into a store this
# client never reads. Unset, it defaults to the public delegated-ipfs.dev,
# which will not see records this stack publishes.
VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS=http://localhost:3001

# Optional content-read accelerator, deliberately left unset: dormant is the
# fail-closed state, and a blank value must land there rather than configuring
# a gateway whose every request fails. Uncomment to point it at the compose
# Kubo gateway — but leave it absent rather than blank if you do not want it.
# VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL=http://localhost:8080

# Optional comma-separated public gateways the engine may read from.
# VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS=

# Web3Auth Core Kit. Interactive login needs both. A clean checkout carries
# neither, so the UI renders but cannot create a session until they are set.
# VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID=
# VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER=

aiTitle: Set up cipher-box PR environment for UAT

content.text:
The stack is up and the PR's new specs pass locally. Here is the state and the UAT script.

## What runs now

| Service | Address | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web, e2e bundle (has the console hook) | http://localhost:4173 | use this one for the UAT |
| Web, shipping bundle (no hook) | http://localhost:4174 | interactive login only |
| API | http://localhost:3000 | `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api dev`, pid 35852 |
| Mock `/routing/v1` store | http://localhost:3001 | host process, see the fix below |
| Kubo API / gateway | http://127.0.0.1:5001, http://127.0.0.1:8080 | docker, already up |
| Postgres | localhost:5432 | docker, migrations current |

I checked out `ci/web-e2e-write-path-and-cargo-cache-seed` at `71e1d1405` in the main tree. Your previous branch was `claude/cipher-box-1261-desktop-frontend`, and it is clean.

I ran the PR's new suite against this stack: **5 of 5 write-path specs pass** in 4.6 s.

## One repo defect blocked the stack

The `cipherbox-mock-ipns-routing` container was a stale image that sends no CORS headers, so every IPNS resolve from the browser failed with `net::ERR_FAILED` and all 5 specs timed out. A rebuild fails too: `docker/../tools/mock-ipns-routing/Dockerfile:12` runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which exits 1 on `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS: esbuild@0.28.2`. I stopped the container and run `node tools/mock-ipns-routing/dist/index.js` on the host instead, which is what CI does. Tell me if you want an issue for the broken Dockerfile.

I also added `http://localhost:4173` and `http://localhost:4174` to `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in `apps/api/.env`.

## The manual UAT — issue #1247

The PR comment names one claim that only a human at a browser can settle: does an ordinary browser save the **file's own bytes**, or the app shell? The trap is that the buffered path also works, so a run that silently takes it proves nothing.

Open http://localhost:4173 in Chrome with DevTools open.

**Step 1 — create a session.** Google login needs a real account. The console hook is faster:

```js
const s = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
const hex = Array.from(s, b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
await window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__.signIn(hex);
```

A fresh secret makes a fresh vault. I ran this snippet here and it reaches `/files`.

**Step 2 — prove the worker controls the page.** Run this before any click:

```js
navigator.serviceWorker.controller !== null   // must be true
(await navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations()).map(r => [r.scope, r.active?.scriptURL, r.active?.state])
// expect ["http://localhost:4173/", ".../sw.js", "activated"]
```

If the controller is `null`, reload once and check again. A false value means `MediaService.streaming` is false, `streamTicket` returns null, and `save` takes the buffered blob path (`apps/web/src/lib/streamTicket.ts:14`). That path works and settles nothing.

**Step 3 — upload a file.** Use a file of a few KB with bytes you can recognize. Copy the row's `data-node-id` — that is the node hex.

**Step 4 — click Download with the Network tab filtered on `stream`.** Read the outcome:

- **Stream path, correct:** a request to `/stream/<uuid>`, status 200 or 206, with `cache-control: no-store`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `accept-ranges: bytes`.
- **The bug (#1247):** a `/stream/<uuid>` response of `content-type: text/html`, 394 bytes, without those headers. The origin answered with the SPA fallback. I confirmed with curl that the preview server returns exactly that for `/stream/<anything>`, so the worker is the only thing that stops it.
- **Buffered path, inconclusive:** no network request at all, and the anchor href starts with `blob:`. Go back to step 2.

Also watch for `[data-testid="vault-action-error"]` in the page.

**Step 5 — compare the bytes.** The engine's own read is the reference:

```js
await window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__.download('<nodeHex>')   // plaintext as hex
```

Then check the saved file, for example `xxd -p ~/Downloads/<name> | tr -d '\n'`. A 394-byte HTML file is the failure. Equal bytes settle the claim.

The PR body records a second finding you can exercise the same way: a second forced refresh while a pass is in flight displaces it, and the queue then drains on neither.

input.command: B=4128ccca2e4a14a27ade7d1cdcc2df7b9f2bbab4; git diff $B origin/main -- apps/api/.env.example apps/web/.env.example
input.description: Diff the env examples between the merge base and main

content.content:
diff --git a/apps/api/.env.example b/apps/api/.env.example
index aaa74c4c5..0587ec061 100644
--- a/apps/api/.env.example
+++ b/apps/api/.env.example
@@ -36,3 +36,24 @@ KUBO_API_URL=http://localhost:5001
 # 3001 is the compose stack's hermetic record store; someguy on 8190 is the
 # real-DHT alternative. Must match the web app's VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS.
 ROUTING_V1_URL=http://localhost:3001
+
+# Signs the identity token the Core Kit consumes, as base64-encoded PKCS8 PEM
+# (a multiline PEM does not survive a .env file). Unset, development and test
+# mint an ephemeral keypair; every deployed profile refuses to boot without it,
+# because Torus caches the JWKS per URL and a key that changes on restart makes
+# every later login fail verification. Generate with:
+#   openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 | base64 -w0
+# IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=
+
+# The Google OAuth client ID the ID token is minted for — the provider's, NOT
+# the Web3Auth project's. Must match the web app's VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID. The
+# audience check is always enforced; a deployed profile refuses to boot unset.
+# GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
+
+# Delivers the passwordless email code. 'log' prints it to the server log and is
+# refused outside development and test; 'sendgrid' additionally needs
+# SENDGRID_API_KEY and MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS. A deployed profile refuses to boot
+# with none configured, rather than failing at the first send.
+MAIL_PROVIDER=log
+# SENDGRID_API_KEY=
+# MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=noreply@cipherbox.cc
diff --git a/apps/web/.env.example b/apps/web/.env.example
index 0f0fc2076..58e7a85d6 100644
--- a/apps/web/.env.example
+++ b/apps/web/.env.example
@@ -22,7 +22,14 @@ VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS=http://localhost:3001
 # Optional comma-separated public gateways the engine may read from.
 # VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS=
 
-# Web3Auth Core Kit. Interactive login needs both. A clean checkout carries
-# neither, so the UI renders but cannot create a session until they are set.
+# Web3Auth Core Kit. Interactive login needs all three, and a clean checkout
+# carries none — the UI renders but cannot create a session until they are set.
+#
+# The two client IDs are separate registrations and are NOT interchangeable:
+#   VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID — the Web3Auth project, from the Web3Auth dashboard
+#   VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID   — the Google Cloud OAuth 2.0 client the verifier's
+#                             Google sub-verifier is registered against

content.text:
Rebase is done locally and it uncovered a real regression on main. Status:

**The rebase itself is clean.** `git rebase origin/main` replayed all 6 commits; one conflict, in `apps/web/src/engine/introspection.ts` — main's login now imports `handOffLoginSecret` from the new `@cipherbox/login` package, the branch's `download` tap needs `fromHex`. Both imports are kept. Gates after the rebase:

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean (6 projects)
- `pnpm lint` — clean
- `pnpm lint:tracker-refs` — clean, 752 files
- `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web test` — 314 passed
- the diff against main is 10 files and holds only the intended cache keys, workflow and spec changes

**But the PR's own write-path specs fail on the new base.** Same local stack, same specs:

| Head | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `71e1d1405` — pre-rebase | 5 of 5 pass, 5.2 s |
| rebased onto `c27c00b9e` | 5 of 5 fail, 60 s settle timeout each |

I reproduced it by hand in Chrome, outside Playwright: log in, create a folder, force one refresh pass, wait 40 s. The child stays `pending: "metadata"` forever. `deadLetters` is empty, `blocked` is null, staleness is `fresh`, and the footer reads `synced`. The routing store answers every PUT with 200, so records do publish; the queue simply never clears the pending mark. The snapshot reports an all-zero root id. One spec run showed `refresh failed: no endpoint served a record this pass could adopt`.

Main's range added ~1141 lines to `crates/engine/src/sync/provision.rs` plus changes to `session.rs`, `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` and the client worker transport, through #1273, #1276, #1277 and #1279. A sub-agent is tracing the exact gate now.

I did not push the rebase yet. The choice is to push it red, or to land the small adaptation first if the root cause turns out to sit in the branch's login path rather than in the engine. I will report the root cause as soon as the trace lands.

Two more things from the run, both local-stack, not the PR:

- The `cipherbox-mock-ipns-routing` container image was stale and sends no CORS headers, so every browser resolve failed. Its Dockerfile also fails to rebuild (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exits 1 on `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS: esbuild@0.28.2`). I run the store from source on the host instead, as CI does.
- The API's per-IP auth limit is 10/min by default and a full suite run needs 11 logins. I set `THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT=200` in `apps/api/.env`, which is what `web-e2e.yml` uses.

The stack is back up on the rebased head: API on :3000, routing on :3001, e2e bundle on :4173, shipping bundle on :4174.

<result>## Root cause found — it is not provisioning. It is the read accelerator's new session bearer + browser CORS.

I reproduced it live in Chrome against the still-running local stack (web preview :4173, mock routing :3001, Kubo :8080) and traced it to the byte.

### The mechanism (proven, not inferred)

`892ca9981` (in your range) changed the accelerator's credential from *host-configured* to *the live session JWT*:

- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1664` — `gateway: gateway.into_gateway(accelerator_bearer.clone())`, and `:1735` `.with_session_bearer(...)`, so `api.login_identity` at `:1739` fills the same cell.
- `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:219-230` — `into_gateway` attaches that bearer to the accelerator leg **if `carries_credentials_safely`**, and `:176-188` returns `true` for `localhost | 127.0.0.1 | [::1]` — the comment even says "a loopback host for local development (`apps/web/.env.example` ships a `http://localhost` Kubo)".
- `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:382-387` — every block fetch then carries `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`.

At the base commit that bearer was `Option<Zeroizing<String>>` supplied by the host (`git show 4128ccc:crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:68`), and `apps/web/src/engine/config.ts:103-104` never supplied one — so the request went out unauthenticated.

An `Authorization` header makes the cross-origin GET non-simple. Kubo's gateway advertises `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Range, User-Agent, X-Requested-With` — **no `Authorization`**. Measured in the page itself:

```
Accept: application/vnd.ipld.raw               -> 200, 1052 bytes
Accept + Authorization: Bearer x               -> FAIL "Failed to fetch"   (preflight rejected)
```

`VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` is unset in `apps/web/.env`, so the accelerator is the only source (`read.rs:166`, `:315-319` rotates on transport failure — there is nothing to rotate to). Every block read in the browser now fails.

### Answers

1. **No new provisioning gate is failing.** The real gates are: the resolve-tick loop spawns only with a root name (`facade.rs:2192`), and the drain leg runs only when *both* scope seeds are cached (`facade.rs:2388-2390`). Both were satisfied in my repro. What blocks the publish is one step later: `Drain::load_scope_root` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:838-852`) needs the root's head block through the gateway (`assemble_head_envelope`) and returns `Halt::UploadAttempt` when it cannot — silently, no dead letter. The same gateway failure makes `RootAdopter` fail, which the tick maps to `RefreshVerdict::Unreachable` → the exact string you saw (`facade.rs:2640`).

2. **All-zero root id is legitimate.** `facade.rs:1669` seeds `Snapshot::new(NodeId([0u8; 16]))`, and `facade.rs:2227`: "The vault's own root scope and root node are the anchored all-zero id16". It is not an unprovisioned tell.

3. **`handOffLoginSecret` is identical on both paths and the hook is missing no facade call.** Both `packages/login/src/flow.ts` (`handOff`) and `apps/web/src/engine/introspection.ts` call `handOffLoginSecret(facade, exporter)` → `facade.start(secret)` (`packages/login/src/secret.ts:63-73`). Provisioning lives *inside* `start` (`facade.rs:1779`). Live proof: the hook login minted the vault — no `vaultUnprovisioned` event was emitted (the event does cross the bridge: `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:748`), and the mock routing log shows the mint's two PUTs (root record then vault pointer, both 200) followed by the tick loop GETting the root name 200/310 bytes every cadence. The app's own path only adds the API identity exchange before Core Kit; the engine does its own `api.login_identity` either way.

4. **No test can see this.** `crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs:578` builds engines on `ApiBaseUrl::offline()` (which skips provisioning by design, `facade.rs:1776-1779`) and plants records, so "first-run mint → queued write drains" is never composed. The gateway tests use a scripted HTTP fake and assert only that the header is *present* (`read.rs:506` "accelerator request carries the member bearer token"). CORS is browser-only, and the wasm suite's new test just proves a host-supplied bearer is refused (`crates/wasm/src/host.rs`). Your web-e2e write-path specs are the first thing in the repo that could catch it.

5. **Root cause, one sentence:** since `892ca9981` the engine stamps the session JWT onto every read-accelerator request — including a loopback Kubo, which `carries_credentials_safely` explicitly permits — and the browser's CORS preflight for `Authorization` is rejected by that gateway, so no block can be read, the root never adopts, and the drain halts in `load_scope_root` before it publishes.

**Smallest fix — it is main's regression, and the one-liner belongs in `crates/engine`:** in `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:176-188`, stop treating a loopback accelerator as credential-safe (fall to `GatewaySource::public(base_url)`, `read.rs:227`). No browser will ever deliver an `Authorization` header to a plain local gateway, so the loopback exemption can only ever break reads — and it also stops shipping the session token to a gateway that isn't CipherBox's. Staging/prod are `https://` and unaffected.

Caller-side alternatives if you want the loopback exemption kept: move the Kubo URL from `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL` to `VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` in `apps/web/.env`(+`.env.example`, + the web-e2e CI env), or add `Authorization` to Kubo's `Gateway.HTTPHeaders` CORS allowlist in the compose file. Either unblocks the specs, but neither protects the next host that points the accelerator at a gateway it doesn't control.

One thing to check separately: whatever real accelerator staging uses must allowlist `Authorization` in its CORS response, or the web app will fail there the same way.</result>

content.text:
The diagnosis is proven end-to-end. With `Authorization` allowed on the local Kubo gateway, the rebased head passes **11 of 11** e2e specs in 5.5 s — the same head that failed 5 of 5 minutes earlier.

**Root cause.** `892ca9981` (#1243, in the rebase range) sources the read-accelerator bearer from the session. `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:174-189` treats a loopback accelerator as credential-safe, so the engine stamps `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on every block read to `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. That makes the request non-simple, and Kubo's gateway advertises no `Authorization` in `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`, so the browser preflight rejects it. No block reads, the root never adopts, and `Drain::load_scope_root` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:838-852`) halts before it publishes — with no dead letter, which is why the UI reads `synced` while the write sits pending forever.

This hits CI as well: `web-e2e.yml:90` sets `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080` against a stock Kubo service. So the rebased branch fails its own gate until something changes. Two other consequences: the loopback rule sends a session token to any gateway the host does not own, and staging's real accelerator must allow `Authorization` in CORS or the web app fails there the same way.

The rebase is committed locally and unpushed. Where the fix lands decides whether I push now.

input.content:
fix(engine): deny the read-accelerator bearer to a plain-http gateway

The session bearer reached any loopback accelerator, and no browser can
deliver it: `Authorization` makes the cross-origin block read non-simple,
and a stock Kubo gateway's CORS allow-list omits that header, so every
preflight is rejected. With the accelerator the only content source, the
root never adopts and `Drain::load_scope_root` halts before it publishes —
a queued write stays pending with no dead letter and the chrome still
reads `synced`.

TLS is now the whole rule. A leg denied the token still serves reads
unauthenticated, which is what a local Kubo needs, and the token stops
reaching a gateway the host does not own.

The web e2e write path is what catches this: the engine's own gateway
tests drive a scripted HTTP fake, and CORS exists only in a browser.

input.content:
Since #1243 the engine stamps the member's session JWT onto every read-accelerator request, and `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs` treats a loopback accelerator as able to keep it:

```rust
matches!(host, "localhost" | "127.0.0.1" | "[::1]")
```

No browser can deliver that header to such a gateway. `Authorization` makes the cross-origin block read non-simple, and a stock Kubo gateway answers the preflight with

```
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Range, User-Agent, X-Requested-With
```

which omits it. Measured in the page against the local stack:

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `Accept: application/vnd.ipld.raw` | 200, 1052 bytes |
| the same plus `Authorization: Bearer …` | `Failed to fetch` — preflight rejected |

## What it breaks

`VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` is unset in `apps/web/.env`, so the accelerator is the only content source and there is nothing to rotate to. Every block read fails, so:

- the root never adopts, and the resolve tick reports `RefreshVerdict::Unreachable` — the chrome shows `refresh failed: no endpoint served a record this pass could adopt`
- `Drain::load_scope_root` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:838-852`) cannot assemble the head envelope and returns `Halt::UploadAttempt`, so a queued write never publishes

The write stays `pending` with **no dead letter**, and the status indicator still reads `synced`. A cold start to an empty vault still works, which is why the smoke tier never saw it.

## Reproduction

Against the local stack with `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080`: log in, create a folder, force one refresh pass, wait. The child stays `pending: "metadata"` forever. Allowing `Authorization` in that Kubo's `Gateway.HTTPHeaders` makes the same build pass 11 of 11 web e2e specs.

## Why no test caught it

`crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` builds engines on `ApiBaseUrl::offline()` and plants records, so "first-run mint then a queued write drains" is never composed. The gateway tests drive a scripted HTTP fake and assert only that the header is present. CORS exists only in a browser, so the web e2e write path is the first suite in the repo that can catch this class.

## Fix

TLS is the whole rule: a plain-http accelerator falls to `GatewaySource::public` and still serves reads, unauthenticated. That also stops the session token reaching a gateway the host does not own.

## Related, not covered here

Whatever accelerator staging points at must list `Authorization` in its CORS allow-list, or the deployed web app fails the same way.

content.content:
lockfile changes. macOS, Windows and the desktop matrix are deliberately not
seeded: they would add four more multi-GB entries on the most expensive runners.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` — all clean.
- `zizmor --no-online-audits .github/workflows/ .github/actions/` (the pinned
  1.25.2) — no findings; the new workflow is not added to any ignore list.
- `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e --repeat-each=6` against a live
  local stack — 78 passed.

## Found on the way, not fixed here

Two runtime findings outside this PR's files, both reproducible:

- **Saving a file to disk silently writes the wrong bytes.** `useFileDownload`
  mints a `/stream/<ticket>` URL and clicks an anchor at it; the Service Worker
  does not intercept that request, so the origin answers with the SPA fallback
  and the user gets a 394-byte `index.html` under the file's name, with no error
  surfaced. Reproduced 3/3. This is why the round trip asserts through the
  preview — the buffered read — rather than through the save.
- **A second forced refresh while a pass is in flight displaces it**, and the
  queue drains on neither; polling the footer's refresh control at 1 Hz kept a
  single queued folder create unpublished for over 60 s, while one click settles
  it in ~1.8 s. The suite works around it by forcing exactly one pass and then
  waiting passively.

Also worth wiring by whoever owns `apps/web`: `engineHostConfig` never sets
`profile`, so a `VITE_ENVIRONMENT=ci` bundle runs the production 30 s poll
cadence rather than the CI profile's 1 s. That is what makes the forced-pass
workaround necessary at all.

## The engine defect the new suite caught

The rebase onto main turned all five write specs red, and the cause is #1280,
not the rebase. Since #1243 the engine hands the member's session JWT to any
loopback read accelerator. No browser can deliver it: `Authorization` makes the
cross-origin block read non-simple, and a stock Kubo gateway's CORS allow-list
omits that header, so every preflight is rejected. With `VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS`
unset the accelerator is the only content source, so no block reads at all — the
root never adopts and `Drain::load_scope_root` halts before it publishes. The
write stays pending with **no dead letter** while the chrome still reads
`synced`, which is why the smoke tier never saw it.

`carries_credentials_safely` now admits TLS and nothing else. A leg denied the
token still serves reads unauthenticated, which is what a local Kubo needs, and
the token stops reaching a gateway the host does not own.

This is the class the tier exists for: the engine's gateway tests drive a
scripted HTTP fake, `write_plane.rs` builds on `ApiBaseUrl::offline()` and
plants records, and CORS exists only in a browser.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` — all clean.
- `zizmor --no-online-audits .github/workflows/ .github/actions/` (the pinned
  1.25.2) — no findings; the new workflow is not added to any ignore list.
- `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine` — 977 unit plus every integration target,
  green; `cargo clippy -p cipherbox-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e` against a live local stack whose
  Kubo carries the stock CORS allow-list — 13 passed. The same stack on the
  pre-fix head fails all five write specs.
- `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e --repeat-each=6` against a live
  local stack — 78 passed (before the rebase).

This one is not optional either: the drain's rebase leg reads the record head block back before it publishes onto it, and with no content source configured the queue never drains at all. It is addressed as `127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`, because Kubo serves `localhost` as a *subdomain* gateway and 301s every path request to `.ipfs.localhost`, which resolves nowhere in a browser. Five new specs in `tests/web-e2e/tests/write-path.spec.ts`, bound to shipped `data-testid`s and shipped accessible names — folder create, rename, move and delete, and an upload read back byte for byte through the preview. Two deliberate shapes: - Every case ends on a **drained queue with no dead letter**. "The row is on screen" is the optimistic overlay and would pass over a write that never published. - Each assertion queues a **probe folder behind the write under test**. The op queue is strict FIFO, so the probe's pending mark clears only once everything ahead of it published — otherwise a delete or a move out takes its own row off the root and leaves the settle nothing to wait on. The `e2e` project now takes every spec except the bundle-shape one, so a new spec joins the gate the day it lands instead of when someone remembers to widen a list. `retries: 0` is untouched: the suite ran 78/78 green locally across six repeats of the full file. `tests/web-e2e/README.md` loses the "does not cover yet" section, which is now false, and its local recipe gains Kubo and both variables. ## Seeding the cargo caches from main `ci.yml` triggers on `pull_request` only, and GitHub scopes a cache entry to the ref that wrote it, so every PR's first cargo run was cold on every cargo job. A run *can* read entries scoped to the default branch, so a new `Cargo Cache Seed` workflow writes two of them on main-push and the PR jobs gain a trailing restore-key that reaches them: | seed entry | serves | | --- | --- | | `main-cargo-` | `linux-cargo-`, `core-kats-cargo-`, `client-browser-cargo-` | | `main-wasm-cargo-` | `wasm-engine-cargo-`, `web-e2e-cargo-` | Two entries rather than one per job prefix, because the repo's cache budget is already over the limit and these have to earn their bytes against the PR-scoped entries LRU evicts. <result>## Review: `5dfc33553` — accelerator bearer narrowed to `https://`

Verdict: the narrowing is sound and I found **no path where the session token reaches plaintext transport**. Three real gaps, none of them a token-disclosure bug; the most important one is that the fix does not cover the deployed configuration.

### 1. Downgrade paths — clean

- **Redirects are closed at both seams**, so a `https://` → `http://` hop cannot replay the header: `crates/desktop-seams/src/http.rs:38` (`redirect::Policy::none()`), `packages/client/src/seams/http.ts:29` (`redirect: 'error'`). - **Casing / whitespace / scheme-relative all fail closed.** `HTTPS://`, `" https://…"`, `//gw`, `https:/gw` all miss the prefix at `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:178` → the leg is rebuilt via `GatewaySource::public` (`read.rs:218`) and never armed. - **Denial is permanent.** `GatewaySource::public` mints a *fresh* cell (`read.rs:146-151`); `SessionBearer::set` is `pub(crate)` and only `ApiClient::with_session_bearer` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1735`) ever writes, into the clone the facade holds (`facade.rs:1651-1665`). A denied leg has no path to being armed by a later login.

### 2. Prefix vs. parse

The prefix is the **right** primitive here, and a URL parse would be strictly *worse*: RFC 3986 schemes are case-insensitive, so a parser would accept `HTTPS://gw.test` and hand it the token, where the prefix denies it. Every parser-vs-prefix divergence I can construct lands on the fail-closed side.

The one input that gets through and probably should not: `REDACTED` passes `read.rs:178` and is handed the bearer. Not a downgrade (still TLS to `gw.cipherbox.test`), and the browser `Request` constructor throws `TypeError` on a credentialed URL so it bricks rather than leaks — but reqwest will send it as Basic auth alongside the JWT. Worth an explicit reject on `@` in the authority, or accept it deliberately and pin it in the test.

### 3. Credential leakage in the read path — clean

`SessionBearer`'s hand-written `Debug` redacts (`read.rs:122-130`); `HttpRequest`'s `Debug` renders header *names* only (`crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs:57-67`); `InvalidBearer` carries nothing (`http.rs:31-33`); the `fetch` refusal string is a static literal (`read.rs:375-377`). Headers are rebuilt per source inside `fetch` (`read.rs:371`), so nothing is retained across a rotation, and `GatewaySource::public` fallbacks hold an unarmable cell. `HttpCredentials::Omit` is pinned on the gateway leg (`read.rs:385`).

### 4. Privacy

An unauthenticated accelerator read exposes **strictly less**: without the JWT the operator sees CIDs + IP + SNI, with it they also get account linkage plus a token that authorizes the whole API. The delta runs the other way — see gap B.

Standing risk this change does not touch: the accelerator is CipherBox's own token-authed Kubo (`CONTEXT.md:81`), and it receives the *full-API* session JWT. A gateway compromise is a session takeover for every online member. TLS is not the mitigation for that; an audience-scoped gateway token is.

---

### Gap A (highest value) — the fix does not cover staging

The commit's stated root cause is CORS, which is **scheme-independent**, but the fix keys on scheme. The read accelerator in staging is a token-authed Kubo behind TLS. ### Gap B — the downgrade is silent, and it can widen the CID audience

`into_gateway` (`read.rs:209-221`) emits no event when it denies the token. If the configured accelerator *requires* auth, every block read now 401s and rotates to `public_fallbacks` — handing the member's read CID set to a third-party gateway that previously never saw it, with no event and no dead letter. That is the same fail-quiet shape the commit message calls out on the write path. Harmless in the shipped local config (`VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` empty) but not in a real deployment. Recommend surfacing the denial once at construction.

`GatewaySource.bearer` is `pub` (`read.rs:141`) and `Gateway.accelerator` is `pub`, so `carries_credentials_safely` guards exactly one call site. Any future in-crate `GatewaySource { base_url, bearer }` bypasses it silently. Make it structural:

```rust
impl GatewaySource {
    /// The only way to attach a credential: TLS or no token.
    pub fn accelerator(base_url: impl Into<String>, bearer: SessionBearer) -> Self {
        let base_url = base_url.into();
        if carries_credentials_safely(&base_url) { Self { base_url, bearer } }

    }

```

Neither updated test is vacuous — `SessionBearer::holding` starts held, so both `is_held()` / `!is_held()` assertions have real polarity. But both are **config-level only**: the doc comment's claim that "a leg denied the token still serves reads, unauthenticated" is never asserted on the wire. The only wire-level no-`AUTHORIZATION` assertion is on the *public fallback* leg (`read.rs:643-648`), not on a denied accelerator.

```rust

    for base_url in ["HTTPS://gw.cipherbox.test", "Https://gw.cipherbox.test",

}

#[test]

// The doc comment's second half, asserted on the wire rather than the config.

fn a_plain_http_accelerator_is_still_consulted_and_carries_no_authorization() {
    // GatewayConfig { accelerator: Some("http://127.0.0.1:8080"), .. }
    // -> read_block -> requests()[0].url starts with the accelerator
    // -> and no AUTHORIZATION header
}

// Denial survives a later login (facade-level).

fn a_login_after_construction_cannot_arm_a_plain_http_accelerator() {}

<result>Security review of `5dfc33553` — findings below. Two real issues, both in comments/framing rather than behavior; the code change itself is sound.

## 1. Fail-closed behaviour — holds

Verification is entirely independent of the bearer. The bearer only affects header construction in `fetch` (`crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:369-376`); every trust check runs after, on the response body:

- Pre-fetch anchor rejection: `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:296-299` (`is_plane_anchor` → `TrustViolation::ContentCidMismatch`).
- Tampered block still rejected: `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:333-335` — `verify_cid(expected_cid, &response.body).map_err(ReadError::TrustViolation)`, terminal, no rotation. Covered by `tampered_bytes_fail_closed_as_a_trust_violation` at `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:500-526`.
- The distinction survives downstream mapping: `crates/engine/src/net/adopter.rs:554-561` and `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:163-168` both keep `TrustViolation` separate from `Unavailable`/`TooLarge`.

**A denied credential is NOT distinguishable from an availability failure.** Every non-2xx — 401/403 included — hits the bare `continue` at `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:320-322` and the exhausted set surfaces as `ReadError::Unavailable` (`:339`). That is the correct trust verdict (a 401 is not an integrity signal), but it means an accelerator that *requires* auth over plain http is now permanently unreachable and reports only a generic "block unavailable". In the drain that collapses further: `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:853` maps *any* head-assembly error to `Halt::UploadAttempt`, a charged retry with no operator-visible reason. No trust regression; a diagnosability gap.

## 2. No deployment loses acceleration

Every accelerator that is actually configured anywhere is a local Kubo that requires no auth:

- `.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml:95` — `http://127.0.0.1:8080`
- `tests/web-e2e/README.md:65` — same
- `apps/web/.env.example:20` — `http://localhost:8080`, commented out

input.content:
refactor(engine): make the accelerator credential rule structural

The rule guarded one call site, and both `GatewaySource` fields are public,
so a later in-crate literal would arm a leg silently. `GatewaySource::accelerator`
is now the only way a source receives the bearer.

An `REDACTED` authority is denied too: reqwest would send the
embedded pair as Basic auth beside the bearer.

Three tests follow the rule rather than the old loopback carve-out: the
uppercase and padded scheme forms a URL parser would accept as TLS, the
credentialed authority, and a wire-level pass proving a denied accelerator is
still the first source consulted and sends no `Authorization`.
